title: Obotrites
capsule: The Obotrites were a confederation of West Slavic tribes occupying modern Mecklenburg and eastern Holstein, east of the Limes Saxoniae, who appear in Frankish sources from the late eighth century as Carolingian allies against the Saxons and Danes. Charlemagne employed Obotrite forces at the Battle of Bornhöved (798), where they defeated the Danes and helped secure the northern frontier; their prince Thrasco was murdered at Danish instigation in 809. Through the ninth century their princes—Slavomir, Ceadrag, and others—oscillated between Frankish vassalage and revolt, frequently allying with the Danes against the empire. By the mid-tenth century the confederation under Nako faced renewed pressure from the Ottonian Saxons advancing eastward across the Elbe.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The general area of Obotrite settlement in Mecklenburg is well established from Frankish annals and archaeological evidence; internal tribal divisions and shifting boundaries of confederation control are poorly mapped and change substantially over the attestation period.
